lines.text: You've already forgiven them. So why forgive once more?
Two people after a fight, sitting back to back. Neither will speak first.
Two families, one old grudge, decades of hatred.
Two programs on a screen. You hit me, I hit you back.
Peter once asked: Lord, how many times should I forgive? Seven times?
Jesus answered: not seven times, but seventy times seven.
Scientists have simulated this on computers: two programs, meeting again and again.
The intuitive strategy is tit for tat. Whatever you do to me, I do to you.
But one misunderstanding, one kind move mistaken for an attack,
and the revenge begins. You strike back, I strike back, and it never stops.
Another program is different. Now and then, it forgives once more.
That one extra chance pulls them both out of the spiral. In the long run, it goes further.
Game theory only echoes one thing: forgiveness is not naive.
And forgiveness in the Bible was never a calculation.
Of course, this assumes the other person is still in the relationship. Being hurt doesn't mean enduring forever.
So once more isn't another retreat. It's one more chance for the relationship.
If it were you, would you give them one more chance?

t2i: A wide, distant view of a long empty park bench running horizontally across the lower third of the frame. On the left end sits a woman in her thirties in a light grey knit sweater with dark hair tied in a low ponytail, seen in side profile facing the left edge of the frame; on the right end sits a broad-shouldered man in his forties in a dark navy jacket with short cropped hair, seen in side profile facing the right edge, so they sit back to back with the long empty middle of the bench between them. Both are seen from a distance, faces turned away.
A bare tree branch reaches in from the upper right corner; a plain path and flat grass fill the ground. The upper half of the frame is open, quiet space.
bench_apart.scene: Two people sit back to back at the two ends of a long park bench, with empty space between them
bench_apart.ident: Preserve a woman in her thirties in a light grey knit sweater with dark hair tied in a low ponytail on the left end and a broad-shouldered man in his forties in a dark navy jacket with short cropped hair on the right end, both facing away from each other, the bench, the tree branch and the empty middle of the frame
acts: Both stay seated and still, backs to each other.
Each lowers the head slightly, a small heavy movement; a few dry leaves drift down between them.
bench_apart.camera: Static wide shot, locked-off, no camera movement.

t2i: A vast hillside landscape. A narrow winding path starts in the lower left foreground and climbs toward the upper right between layered hills, disappearing into soft haze. Far along the path, two small figures walk side by side toward the upper right.
Layered hills fill the middle distance; the upper third of the frame is wide open sky with one thin drifting cloud.
hill_path.scene: A winding hill path climbing toward the upper right, two small figures walking side by side into the haze
hill_path.ident: Preserve the path, the layered hills, the two small figures walking together and the open sky
acts: The two figures walk slowly together along the path toward the upper right; the thin cloud drifts.
They keep walking side by side and grow smaller in the haze.
hill_path.camera: Static wide shot, locked-off, no camera movement.

t2i: A medium-wide view of a small kitchen table by a window. A woman in her thirties in a light grey knit sweater with dark hair tied in a low ponytail sits on the left side of the table and a broad-shouldered man in his forties in a dark navy jacket with short cropped hair sits on the right side, facing each other across it, seen in side view, faces turned slightly down. On the table are two plain mugs of tea; thin steam rises from the mug on the left.
Behind them a plain wall and a window with soft daylight. The upper third of the frame is quiet empty wall.
kitchen_table.scene: Two people sit facing each other across a small kitchen table, steam rising from one mug
kitchen_table.ident: Preserve a woman in her thirties in a light grey knit sweater with dark hair tied in a low ponytail on the left and a broad-shouldered man in his forties in a dark navy jacket with short cropped hair on the right, the table, both mugs and the window
acts: Thin steam rises slowly from the left mug and curls upward. Both stay seated and still.
The man lowers his head slightly; neither stands up or leaves.
kitchen_table.camera: Static medium-wide shot, locked-off, no camera movement.

t2i: A wide, distant view of the same long park bench running horizontally across the lower third of the frame. On the left end sits a woman in her thirties in a light grey knit sweater with dark hair tied in a low ponytail, now turned toward the right, facing the other end of the bench; on the right end sits a broad-shouldered man in his forties in a dark navy jacket with short cropped hair, still seen in side profile facing the right edge. Both are seen from a distance.
Between them the long empty middle of the bench. A bare tree branch reaches in from the upper right corner; a plain path and flat grass fill the ground.
bench_turn.scene: The same park bench; the woman has turned toward the man, who still faces away
bench_turn.ident: Preserve a woman in her thirties in a light grey knit sweater with dark hair tied in a low ponytail on the left end, a broad-shouldered man in his forties in a dark navy jacket with short cropped hair on the right end, the bench and the tree branch
acts: The man slowly turns his head a little toward the woman.
He shifts his shoulders slightly toward her; both stay seated on the bench.
bench_turn.camera: Static wide shot, locked-off, no camera movement.
